hints: Focus on what heating with aqueous acid does, it adds water across certain bonds in a hydrolysis reaction.
Identify each functional group first: 1 is an aldehyde, 2 is a nitrile, and 3 is an ester.
Recall which two groups hydrolyse in acid to give a carboxylic acid, and check if the two-carbon fragment matches ethanoic acid.
walkthrough:
**Name the three functional groups**

Look carefully at what is attached to the $\text{CH}_3$ group in each structure. Compound 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, ethanal (an aldehyde). Compound 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$, ethanenitrile (a nitrile). Compound 3 is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_3$, methyl ethanoate (an ester).

**Recall acid hydrolysis reactions**

Both nitriles and esters are hydrolysed when heated with aqueous acid to give carboxylic acids.

For a nitrile:
$$\text{R-CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{HCl(aq), heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

For an ester:
$$\text{R-COOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{HCl(aq), heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Apply to compounds 2 and 3**

For compound 2, $\text{R}$ is $\text{CH}_3$, so the product is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, ethanoic acid. For compound 3, $\text{R}$ is also $\text{CH}_3$, so the acid part again gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ plus methanol. Both 2 and 3 work.

**Check compound 1**

Aldehydes do not hydrolyse with $\text{HCl(aq)}$. Ethanal can be oxidised to ethanoic acid with an oxidising agent, but aqueous $\text{HCl}$ is not an oxidant, it is just an acid catalyst for hydrolysis. So 1 does not give ethanoic acid here.

options.A: Incorrect. While 2 and 3 do give ethanoic acid by acid hydrolysis, 1 does not. Ethanal is an aldehyde and is not hydrolysed by HCl(aq).
options.B: Incorrect. Compound 2 is correct because ethanenitrile hydrolyses to ethanoic acid, but compound 1 is wrong. Students choosing this may confuse oxidation of an aldehyde with acid hydrolysis.
options.C: Incorrect. Compound 3 is correct because methyl ethanoate hydrolyses to ethanoic acid and methanol, but compound 1 is wrong. An aldehyde plus aqueous acid gives no reaction to form a carboxylic acid.
options.D: Correct. Compound 2 (ethanenitrile) undergoes acid hydrolysis to ethanoic acid and ammonium ions, and compound 3 (methyl ethanoate) undergoes acid hydrolysis to ethanoic acid and methanol. Compound 1 (ethanal) does not react this way.
